chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from al-Ḥasan ibn al-Jahm, who said:

I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام had known his killer, and the night in which he would be killed, and the place in which he would be killed, and his saying when he heard the cries of the geese in the house: “Screaming ones, to be followed by wailing ones.”

And the saying of Umm Kulthūm: “If only you would pray tonight inside the house and order someone else to lead the people in salat (prayer),” but he refused her, and his going in and out frequently that night without a weapon, while he عليه السلام knew that Ibn Muljam—may Allah curse him—was his killer by the sword. Was this among that to which it was not permissible for him to expose himself?
So he عليه السلام said: “That was so, but he was given the choice on that night so that the decrees of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, might come to pass.”

key_terms.اللَّيْلَةَ: the specific night of the foretold martyrdom
key_terms.الْمَوْضِعَ: the place where the killing would occur
key_terms.بِلَا سِلَاحٍ: without a weapon; indicating his outward state that night
key_terms.صَوَائِحُ: those crying out or shrieking; here referring to ominous cries
key_terms.قَاتِلَهُ: his killer; the one who would murder him
key_terms.مَقَادِيرُ: the divine decrees or ordained measures

ai.seo_question: Did Imām ʿAlī عليه السلام know the time and place of his martyrdom, and how does that relate to divine decree?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the foreknowledge of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding his martyrdom and asks how this relates to his outward conduct on that night. Imām al-Riḍā عليه السلام replies that this indeed was the case, but that he was given a choice so that the divine decrees of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would be fulfilled.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Hameed, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jahm who said,

‘I said to Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> had recognised his<sup>asws</sup> murderer and the night in which he<sup>asws</sup> would be murdered, and the place in which he<sup>asws</sup> would be murdered, and his<sup>asws</sup> words to what he<sup>asws</sup> heard the shrieking of the geese in the house: ‘Their shrieking would be followed by their wailing’,

and the words of Umm Kulsoum: ‘If youasws could pray the night inside the house and order someone else to pray Salat with the people’, so heasws refused upon it, and used to frequently enter it and exit from it during that night without a weapon, and heasws had recognised that Ibn Muljimla, may Allahazwj Curse himla, would kill himasws with the sword. This was from what it is not allowed to be exposed to’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That was so, but it was better during that night for the accomplishment of the Pre-determination of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid from al-Hassan ibn al-Jahm who has said that he said to al-Rida (a.s.) the following.

“Amir al-Mu’minin Ali (a.s.) knew his assassin, the night in of being murdered and the spot whereat who be murdered. It is his words on hearing the ducks at the house, “These are the quacks that will be followed by lamentations.”

Also the words of ’Umm Kulthum (his daughter). “Would that you pray inside the house and send someone else to lead the prayer in the Mosque.” He refused to do so and at that night he went many times out of the house unarmed. He knew that ibn Muljim, may he be condemned will murder him with a sword. He must not have exposed himself to it”
The Imam (a.s.) said, “It is true but it was chosen that night wherein the measure and the determination of Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High would come to pass.”
